meta.name: What is FrameTrail?
meta.description: The front page of frametrail.org as a film without video: what FrameTrail is, its features, use cases and principles, in the page's own words, each with a small demonstration.
meta.creator: demo

frametrail:attributes.text: <p><span style="font-size: 22px;">FrameTrail is an open source software that lets you experience, manage and edit interactive video directly in your web browser.</span></p>

body.frametrail:name: What you can do with it

frametrail:attributes.text: <p><span style="font-size: 22px;">Add multimedia overlays, annotations or clickable links to any video — or create time-based presentations without video at all. All data is stored as portable JSON files.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">Use any video or even an empty canvas with just a duration as a basis for synchronizing contents (like interactive transcripts, overlays or annotation timelines).</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">Create non-linear networks of videos which are connected via clickable hotspots and can be freely navigated by the user (like branching narratives or interactive explainer videos).</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">Place documents on top of the video (e.g. text, images, web pages, interactive maps or custom text/html) and decide how and when they should be displayed.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">Add supplementing materials at certain points of time and decide how they should be displayed in the player using the interactive layout editor.</span></p>
<p style="text-align: right;"><span style="font-family: 'Courier New'; font-size: 13px; color: #6C6F78;">3:18</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 22px;">Film shall be "programmed" with Open Web Technologies, rather than rendered out of an editing interface</span></p>

body.frametrail:name: Tile: Player and Editor are one
Open tile: Player and Editor are one

frametrail:attributes.text: <p><span style="font-size: 16px;">By "rendering" a film, we permanently seal it and "burn" all its fragments (media assets, cuts, text overlays, effects, animations) irreversibly into one flat video file. With FrameTrail, we do the opposite: we create a permanently open format, which can be viewed, remixed and edited forever in any web browser.</span></p>

body.frametrail:name: Player and Editor are one: text

frametrail:attributes.text: <p><span style="font-size: 16px;">No separation of editor and viewer / player. Yes, that means anyone can edit any FrameTrail hypervideo anywhere. Changes can be saved directly (if you have the editing rights), downloaded or exported to another FrameTrail installation. Every hypervideo comes bundled with FrameTrail itself. If you can view it, you can edit it.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">All data is stored as JSON files - no database. Copy the entire data folder to move your instance between servers.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 14px; color: #6C6F78;">rendered: one flat video file</span></p>

frametrail:attributes.text: <p><span style="font-size: 16px;">The way you use, arrange and display the different components of FrameTrail is up to you and the affordances of your project. From just using FrameTrail as a full-site video player up to using it as a highly interactive hypervideo solution, everything is dynamically configurable.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">Multiple hypervideos can be connected via a customizable overview map or grid view, which serves as an entry point to a project and allows easy navigation.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 16px;">To help you get started we've put together several step-by-step tutorials on all aspects of FrameTrail. Just choose one of the links:</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 16px; color: #CCCCD5;">Are you a developer and want to remix / improve / extend this software? Please head over to the Contributors Guide.</span></p>
